## Exploring the Data

NOTE: These tables aren't perfect/are drafts and were done to brainstorm how to frame our findings.

```{r include=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
# Loading necessary libraries
library(haven)
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)
library(scales)
library(labelled)
```

```{r}
# Reading in the data
data <- read_dta("C:/Users/chris/Downloads/covadj_review_final.dta")
head(data)
```

```{r}
# Create a cleaned version with recoded values
data_cleaned <- data %>%
  mutate(
    # Convert labelled variables to factors with proper labels
    rzvarsyesno_clean = case_when(
      rzvarsyesno == 1 ~ "Yes",
      rzvarsyesno == 0 ~ "No",
      TRUE ~ "Unclear"
    ),
    
    # Baseline outcome reported
    baseoutcome_clean = case_when(
      baseoutcome == 1 ~ "Yes",
      baseoutcome == 0 ~ "No",
      TRUE ~ "Unclear"
    ),
    
    # Adjusted for baseline outcome
    baseoutcomeadj_clean = case_when(
      baseoutcomeadj == 1 ~ "Yes",
      baseoutcomeadj == 0 ~ "No",
      TRUE ~ "Unclear/NA"
    ),
    
    # Any adjusted analysis
    adjcovar_clean = case_when(
      adjcovar == 1 ~ "Yes",
      adjcovar == 0 ~ "No",
      TRUE ~ "Unclear"
    ),
    
    # Pre-specification of covariates
    adjprespec_clean = case_when(
      adjprespec == 1 ~ "Pre-specified a priori",
      adjprespec == 0 ~ "Post-hoc",
      adjprespec == -999 ~ "Not reported/Unclear",
      TRUE ~ "Not reported/Unclear"
    ),
    
    # Journal impact factor category (you'll need to define this based on your data)
    # For now, I'll create a placeholder - adjust based on your actual journal impact data
    high_impact = case_when(
      journal %in% c("The lancet. HIV", "Journal of the American Medical Association", 
                     "The Lancet", "New England Journal of Medicine", "BMJ") ~ "High impact (IF > 10)",
      TRUE ~ "Other journals"
    ),
    
    # Number of clusters category
    cluster_size_category = case_when(
      numberofclustersrandomized <= 10 ~ "Small (≤10 clusters)",
      numberofclustersrandomized <= 50 ~ "Medium (11-50 clusters)",
      numberofclustersrandomized > 50 ~ "Large (>50 clusters)",
      TRUE ~ "Not reported"
    )
  )
```

```{r}
# Table 1: Trial Characteristics
table1 <- data_cleaned %>%
  summarise(
    `Total trials` = as.character(n()),
    `Publication year range` = paste(min(publishedyear, na.rm = TRUE), 
                                      "-", 
                                      max(publishedyear, na.rm = TRUE)),
    `Median publication year` = as.character(median(publishedyear, na.rm = TRUE)),
    `High impact journals` = as.character(sum(high_impact == "High impact (IF > 10)", na.rm = TRUE)),
    `High impact journals (%)` = percent(mean(high_impact == "High impact (IF > 10)", na.rm = TRUE), accuracy = 0.1),
    `Median clusters per trial` = as.character(median(numberofclustersrandomized, na.rm = TRUE)),
    `Range of clusters` = paste(min(numberofclustersrandomized, na.rm = TRUE), 
                                "-", 
                                max(numberofclustersrandomized, na.rm = TRUE)),
    `Trials with primary outcome identified` = as.character(sum(primaryoutcomeident == 1, na.rm = TRUE)),
    `Trials with primary outcome identified (%)` = percent(mean(primaryoutcomeident == 1, na.rm = TRUE), accuracy = 0.1)
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Characteristic", values_to = "Value")

# Create gt table
table1_gt <- table1 %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Table 1. Characteristics of Included Cluster Randomized Trials",
    subtitle = paste("N =", nrow(data_cleaned), "trials")
  ) %>%
  cols_label(
    Characteristic = "Characteristic",
    Value = "Value"
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_column_labels(everything())
  ) %>%
  tab_options(
    table.font.size = "small",
    heading.title.font.size = "medium",
    heading.subtitle.font.size = "small"
  )

# Print table
table1_gt
```

Why this table matters for covariate adjustment: (1) publication year range shows whether we're capturing recent practice, (2) journal impact factor could matter a lot (maybe high impact journals are more reliable), (3) primary outcome identification matters because we need to know if trials clearly specified outcomes to assess whether adjustment was pre-specified.

It answers a question: is our sample representative, and do characteristics that might influence covariate handling across trials?

```{r warning=FALSE}
# Table 2: Use of covariates in randomization
# Create denominator for location and size
trials_with_location <- data_cleaned %>%
  filter(!is.na(q4selectcountryorcountriesinwhi) & q4selectcountryorcountriesinwhi != "")

trials_with_variable_size <- data_cleaned %>%
  filter(!is.na(numberofclustersrandomized) & numberofclustersrandomized != 999)

# Create the table data
table2_data <- data.frame(
  review_item = c(
    "Any covariate used in randomization",
    "Type of covariate used (excluding location and size):",
    "  - Cluster-level only",
    "  - Individual-level only",
    "  - Both cluster- and individual-level",
    "  - None",
    "  - Unclear",
    "Covariates used in randomization:",
    "  - Cluster location",
    "  - Cluster size",
    "Number of covariates used (when any used):",
    "  - 1 covariate",
    "  - 2 covariates",
    "  - 3 or more covariates"
  ),
  
  n = c(
    sum(data_cleaned$rzvarsyesno == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    NA,
    sum(data_cleaned$adjcovartype___1 == 1 & 
          (data_cleaned$adjcovartype___2 != 1 | is.na(data_cleaned$adjcovartype___2)), 
        na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(data_cleaned$adjcovartype___2 == 1 & 
          (data_cleaned$adjcovartype___1 != 1 | is.na(data_cleaned$adjcovartype___1)), 
        na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(data_cleaned$adjcovartype___1 == 1 & data_cleaned$adjcovartype___2 == 1, 
        na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(data_cleaned$rzvarsyesno == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(is.na(data_cleaned$rzvarsyesno) | data_cleaned$rzvarsyesno == -999, na.rm = TRUE),
    NA,
    sum(str_detect(data_cleaned$rzvariables, "location"), na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(str_detect(data_cleaned$rzvariables, "size"), na.rm = TRUE),
    NA,
    sum(data_cleaned$rzvarsyesno == 1 & data_cleaned$rzvarsnum == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(data_cleaned$rzvarsyesno == 1 & data_cleaned$rzvarsnum == 2, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(data_cleaned$rzvarsyesno == 1 & data_cleaned$rzvarsnum >= 3, na.rm = TRUE)
  ),
  
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) %>%
  mutate(
    N = case_when(
      review_item == "Any covariate used in randomization" ~ nrow(data_cleaned),
      review_item %in% c("  - Cluster-level only", "  - Individual-level only", 
                         "  - Both cluster- and individual-level", "  - None", "  - Unclear") ~ nrow(data_cleaned),
      review_item == "  - Cluster location" ~ nrow(trials_with_location),
      review_item == "  - Cluster size" ~ nrow(trials_with_variable_size),
      review_item %in% c("  - 1 covariate", "  - 2 covariates", "  - 3 or more covariates") ~ 
        sum(data_cleaned$rzvarsyesno == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    `%` = if_else(is.na(N) | is.na(n), "", sprintf("%.1f%%", (n / N) * 100)),
    `n/N` = if_else(is.na(N) | is.na(n), "", paste0(n, "/", N))
  ) %>%
  select(review_item, `n/N`, `%`)

# Create gt table
table2_gt <- table2_data %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Table 2. Use of Covariates in Randomization",
    subtitle = paste("Based on", nrow(data_cleaned), "cluster randomized trials")
  ) %>%
  cols_label(
    review_item = "Review item",
    `n/N` = "n/N",
    `%` = "%"
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_column_labels(everything())
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(style = "italic"),
    locations = cells_body(rows = c(2, 8, 11))
  ) %>%
  tab_options(
    table.font.size = "small",
    heading.title.font.size = "medium"
  )

table2_gt
```

This table assesses whether researchers are using restricted randomization to promote baseline balance. It highlights type of covariates used, fundamental cluster characteristics (location and size), and number of covariates.

```{r}
# Table 3: Reporting of baseline covariates
# Create the summary data using existing cleaned variables
table3_data <- data.frame(
  review_item = c(
    "Baseline table includes:",
    "  - Cluster-level covariates only",
    "  - Individual-level covariates only",
    "  - Both cluster- and individual-level",
    "  - No table",
    "Baseline measure of primary outcome reported",
    "Significance test of balance reported"
  ),
  
  n = c(
    NA,  # Section header
    sum(data_cleaned$covreportedarm___1 == 1 & 
          (data_cleaned$covreportedarm___2 != 1 | is.na(data_cleaned$covreportedarm___2)), 
        na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(data_cleaned$covreportedarm___2 == 1 & 
          (data_cleaned$covreportedarm___1 != 1 | is.na(data_cleaned$covreportedarm___1)), 
        na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(data_cleaned$covreportedarm___1 == 1 & data_cleaned$covreportedarm___2 == 1, 
        na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(is.na(data_cleaned$covreported) | data_cleaned$covreported == 0, 
        na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(data_cleaned$baseoutcome_clean == "Yes", na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(data_cleaned$baseoutcomenowhy___555 == 555, na.rm = TRUE)
  ),
  
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) %>%
  mutate(
    N = case_when(
      review_item %in% c("Baseline table includes:", "  - Cluster-level covariates only",
                          "  - Individual-level covariates only", "  - Both cluster- and individual-level",
                          "  - No table") ~ nrow(data_cleaned),
      review_item == "Baseline measure of primary outcome reported" ~ nrow(data_cleaned),
      review_item == "Significance test of balance reported" ~ nrow(data_cleaned),
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    `%` = if_else(is.na(N) | is.na(n), "", sprintf("%.1f%%", (n / N) * 100)),
    `n/N` = if_else(is.na(N) | is.na(n), "", paste0(n, "/", N))
  ) %>%
  select(review_item, `n/N`, `%`) 

# Create gt table
table3_gt <- table3_data %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Table 3. Reporting of Baseline Covariates",
    subtitle = paste("Based on", nrow(data_cleaned), "cluster randomized trials")
  ) %>%
  cols_label(
    review_item = "Review item",
    `n/N` = "n/N",
    `%` = "%"
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_column_labels(everything())
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(style = "italic"),
    locations = cells_body(rows = 1)
  ) %>%
  tab_options(
    table.font.size = "small",
    heading.title.font.size = "medium"
  )

# Display the table
table3_gt
```

This table evaluates transparency in reporting what was actually balanced or imbalanced. It answers the question: are trials transparent about baseline comparability?

```{r}
# Table 4: Covariate adjustment in analysis
# Create denominators
trials_with_baseoutcome <- data_cleaned %>% filter(baseoutcome == 1)
trials_with_rzvars <- data_cleaned %>% filter(rzvarsyesno == 1)
trials_with_adj <- data_cleaned %>% filter(adjcovar == 1)

# Create the summary data
table4_data <- data.frame(
  review_item = c(
    "Trial report includes an adjusted analysis",
    "",
    "Adjusted for baseline measure of outcome:",
    "  - Among trials reporting baseline outcome",
    "Adjusted for all covariates used in randomization:",
    "  - Among trials using covariates in randomization",
    "Timing of covariate selection:",
    "  - Pre-specified a priori",
    "  - Post-hoc",
    "  - Unclear/not reported",
    "Level of covariates in adjusted analysis:",
    "  - Cluster-level only",
    "  - Individual-level only",
    "  - Both cluster- and individual-level",
    "  - Unclear"
  ),
  
  n = c(
    sum(data_cleaned$adjcovar == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    NA,
    NA,
    sum(trials_with_baseoutcome$baseoutcomeadj == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    NA,
    sum(trials_with_rzvars$rzvarsused == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    NA,
    sum(data_cleaned$adjprespec == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(data_cleaned$adjprespec == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(data_cleaned$adjprespec == -999 | is.na(data_cleaned$adjprespec), na.rm = TRUE),
    NA,
    sum(data_cleaned$adjcovartype___1 == 1 & 
          (data_cleaned$adjcovartype___2 != 1 | is.na(data_cleaned$adjcovartype___2)), 
        na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(data_cleaned$adjcovartype___2 == 1 & 
          (data_cleaned$adjcovartype___1 != 1 | is.na(data_cleaned$adjcovartype___1)), 
        na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(data_cleaned$adjcovartype___1 == 1 & data_cleaned$adjcovartype___2 == 1, 
        na.rm = TRUE),
    sum((data_cleaned$adjcovartype___1 == 0 | is.na(data_cleaned$adjcovartype___1)) & 
          (data_cleaned$adjcovartype___2 == 0 | is.na(data_cleaned$adjcovartype___2)), 
        na.rm = TRUE)
  ),
  
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) %>%
  mutate(
    N = case_when(
      review_item == "Trial report includes an adjusted analysis" ~ nrow(data_cleaned),
      review_item == "  - Among trials reporting baseline outcome" ~ nrow(trials_with_baseoutcome),
      review_item == "  - Among trials using covariates in randomization" ~ nrow(trials_with_rzvars),
      review_item %in% c("  - Pre-specified a priori", "  - Post-hoc", "  - Unclear/not reported") ~ nrow(trials_with_adj),
      review_item %in% c("  - Cluster-level only", "  - Individual-level only", 
                          "  - Both cluster- and individual-level", "  - Unclear") ~ nrow(trials_with_adj),
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    `%` = if_else(is.na(N) | is.na(n), "", sprintf("%.1f%%", (n / N) * 100)),
    `n/N` = if_else(is.na(N) | is.na(n), "", paste0(n, "/", N))
  ) %>%
  select(review_item, `n/N`, `%`)

# Create gt table
table4_gt <- table4_data %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Table 4. Covariate Adjustment in Analysis of Primary Outcome",
    subtitle = paste("Based on", nrow(data_cleaned), "cluster randomized trials")
  ) %>%
  cols_label(
    review_item = "Review item",
    `n/N` = "n/N",
    `%` = "%"
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_column_labels(everything())
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(style = "italic"),
    locations = cells_body(rows = c(2, 4, 6, 11))
  ) %>%
  tab_options(
    table.font.size = "small",
    heading.title.font.size = "medium"
  )

table4_gt
```

This table assesses whether and how covariates are incorporated into the primary analysis. It asks a question: are researchers adjusting for covariates appropriately, and are they transparent about how they chose which covariates to include?
